question: In karate, the fight starts when the referee shouts “_______”.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Shobu Hajime!**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Shobu Hajime!**

 
 
• In karate, the fight officially begins when the referee shouts **"Shobu Hajime!"**
 
• This phrase translates to "Begin the match!" or "Start the fight!" in English.
 
• It is used in competitive karate to signal the start of a sparring match (kumite).
 
• The referee ensures both competitors are ready before giving this command.
 
• This term is part of the standardized Japanese terminology used in karate competitions worldwide.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Yame**

 
 
• **"Yame"** means "Stop!" in Japanese and is used by the referee to halt the match temporarily.
 
• It is commonly used when a point is scored, a rule is violated, or there is an injury.
 
• After "Yame," the referee may reset the competitors or give instructions before resuming the match.
 
• This command ensures the match is conducted safely and fairly.
 
• It is one of the most frequently used terms during a karate competition.
 
 
 
• **Kaizen**
 
 
• **"Kaizen"** is a Japanese term meaning "continuous improvement" but is not used in karate competitions.
 
• It is more commonly associated with business practices and personal development.
 
• In karate, the focus is on specific commands like "Shobu Hajime" or "Yame" to control the match.
 
• While "Kaizen" reflects the philosophy of self-improvement in martial arts, it is not a referee command.
 
• It is unrelated to the technical terminology used during a karate fight.
 
 
 
• **Yuko**
 
 
• **"Yuko"** is a term used in karate scoring, referring to a mid-level point awarded during a match.
 
• It is given for techniques that demonstrate good form, control, and impact but are less significant than an "Ippon."
 
• A "Yuko" is worth one point in many karate competition formats.
 
• The referee announces "Yuko" when such a technique is successfully executed.
 
• It is not a command to start or stop the match but rather a scoring declaration.
